source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Carrying fairly weak defined purpose within the overall structure of the clinical trial development and approval process","B":"Being the very first time a treatment is ever tested in humans, with a primary focus on establishing its basic safety profile","C":"Occurring mainly after a treatment has already received full regulatory approval from health authorities well beforehand","D":"Compares a new treatment to the current standard of care in a larger population, evaluating efficacy and safety before potential regulatory approval"}}
source_row.rationale: A Phase III clinical trial typically compares a new treatment to the current standard of care in a larger patient population, evaluating both efficacy and safety, representing a later stage of testing that often informs potential regulatory approval decisions, distinct from earlier Phase I trials (which focus primarily on safety in a small population).
